body:
### Problem

parse_cmdline() dereferences NULL when the :tab modifier comes after an address that :tab doesn't accept, such as a mark or a search pattern. nvim crash with SIGSEGV
It can be reached in two ways:
-> vim.api.nvim_parse_cmd("'btab",{})
->Typing :'btab on the command line. Nvim crashes before <CR> is pressed, because the 'inccommand' preview parses the line on every keystroke. With :set inccommand= it doesn’t crash.

More inputs that crash: 'btab, 'atab, '<tab, 'a,'btab, /foo/tab, ?foo?tab, \/tab, \&tab

Found by fuzzing nvim_parse_cmd() with libFuzzer.





What happens, step by step in gdb:

->parse_command_modifiers() matches tab and calls get_address().
->get_address() rejects the mark for ADDR_TABS. It sets eap->cmd = NULL and the error E16: Invalid range.
->parse_command_modifiers() returns FAIL.
->parse_cmdline() only stops when eap->cmd hasn’t moved (after_modifier == orig_cmd, ex_docmd.c:1512). ->So it carries on and passes NULL to find_excmd_after_range() → skip_range().

### Steps to reproduce

nvim --clean
:lua vim.api.nvim_parse_cmd("'btab", {})
Nvim exists with SIGSEGV

or nvim --clean
:'btab
(type it, don’t press <CR>)

### Expected behavior

No crash. nvim_parse_cmd("'btab", {}) should fail with Parsing command-line: E16: Invalid range

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1698+g51d7d99fe7

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

No.

### Operating system/version

Linux x86_64

### Terminal name/version

Not terminal-specific (also reproduces with --headless)

### $TERM environment variable

N/A

### Installation

Build from repo (CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug)
